newsitem.title: USA: S.C. governor proposes bond bank for road work.
newsitem.headline: S.C. governor proposes bond bank for road work.

text.p: South Carolina Gov. David Bealsey proposed creating a Transportation Infrastructure Bank to oversee bond financing for up to $1.5 billion of road and bridge projects in the next six to eight years.
In his state-of-the-state address Wednesday night, Beasley said the bank could start with an $80 million annual budget, enough to allow it to borrow $1.2 billion.

His plan would give the bank one penny of state gas tax that had previously gone to counties, and $21 million of state gas tax revenues that now go into the state's general fund. The bank would also get $12 million a year in interest from the state Highway Fund and $25 million a year from South Carolina's share of federal gas tax revenues.
The money would be used to pay debt service on bonds issued by the bank for road and bridge projects, concentrating on those with statewide economic impact.
"To ensure accountability, I recommend that we create an independent board to oversee the infrastructre bank and the bond proposals," Beasley said.
He said the board's role would also be to protect the state's AAA general obligation bond rating.
"This bank will allow us to tap into the unused bond capacity of the Department of Transportation and come up with more innovating financing options," Beasley said.
"And we can do it without a tax increase," he said.

The Republican governor catalogued his administration's accomplishments in its first two years. He said more than 11,000 families have been moved off the welfare rolls, while tourism has grown to a $13 billion industry that attracts 31 million visitors a year.

"For two straight years, we've broken the $5 billion barrier in capital investment. We've seen a 56 percet rise in job creation over two years, creating 50,000 new jobs with an average salary last year of $30,000," Beasley said.
"Our economy is growing twice as fast as the rest of the nation's and our per-capita income is the eighth fastest growing," Bealsey said. "We're in the best financial shape in our state's history."

The governor also proposed raising teacher salaries, making college tuition more affordable and exempting working senior citizens from paying taxes on their first $50,000 of wage income. The exemption would be phased in over five years.
